title.zh: LLM写作腔：写作中该由谁发声
title.en: LLM Voice: Who Should Write the Prose?

excerpt.zh: LLM写作腔可能让读者感到文字流畅却缺少人的痕迹。Martin Fowler主张作者亲自写正文，同时承认翻译、辅助写作等场景各有取舍。
excerpt.en: LLM voice can make prose feel fluent yet strangely impersonal. Martin Fowler argues that authors should write their own prose, while recognizing meaningful exceptions.

disclosure.zh: 本文使用星期天AI中转站大模型，基于 Hacker News 内容自动生成。
disclosure.en: This article was automatically generated by the Weekly Day AI gateway model using content from Hacker News.

text.zh: LLM写作腔指的是一种让读者觉得文字像由语言模型生成、因而显得不自然的感觉。Martin Fowler认为，这种反应并不总能明确归因于某个词句，却可能削弱读者继续阅读的意愿；检测工具也未必能解决问题，因为读者的感受往往先于检测结果出现。
text.en: LLM voice describes the feeling that prose may have been generated by a language model and therefore sounds unnatural. Martin Fowler argues that readers may not be able to point to a specific phrase, yet the impression can still diminish their desire to continue. Detection tools may not solve the problem: a reader's reaction often arrives before any test result.

text.zh: LLM写作腔为何难以简单判定
text.en: Why LLM voice is hard to identify

text.zh: Fowler提醒，语言习惯会随年代和社群变化，人们熟悉或反感的表达不一定能区分人类与模型写作。因此，他不建议把“听起来像AI”当成可靠判据，也不认为检测器能替代读者对文字的判断。文章关注的核心不是追查作者身份，而是文字是否真正传达了人的思考与个性。
text.en: Fowler cautions that language shifts across generations and communities, so expressions people dislike or find unfamiliar do not reliably distinguish human writing from model output. He therefore treats the impression of sounding like AI as an uncertain signal, and does not see detectors as a substitute for readers' judgment. His central concern is less about proving who wrote a passage than whether it carries a person's thinking and character.
Where AI writing can help, and where it falls short

text.zh: 他建议作者谨慎对待让模型起草正文的做法：即使随后由人修改，原有的表达方式也可能难以彻底改变。他认为让模型协助拟定提纲或许可行，但正文应由作者自己写，并建议披露AI具体如何参与。这个主张有现实边界：他承认，有案例经专业编辑大幅润色后，最终文章没有明显的模型腔。
text.en: He advises caution about asking a model to draft prose: even after human editing, its original manner of expression can be difficult to remove. Using a model to help shape an outline may be acceptable, he suggests, but authors should write the prose themselves and disclose how AI contributed. There are limits to this rule: Fowler notes one case in which substantial professional editing left an AI-written first draft without an obvious model voice.

text.zh: Fowler也承认翻译、辅助残障作者表达、填写例行公文或撰写可能只供流程处理的报告等情境，可能让AI代写更合理。关键在于写作目的：当文字要把一个人的想法传递给另一个人，亲自组织语言也能帮助作者理清思路并持续练习。至于模型日后能否写得让人无法辨别，以及机器可读文档是否会改变这项判断，仍是开放问题。
text.en: Fowler also recognizes cases where AI-generated prose may be reasonable: translation, helping a writer with a disability communicate, routine official correspondence, or reports intended mainly for a process rather than a human reader. Purpose matters. When writing is meant to convey one person's thoughts to another, composing the words can also help the author clarify ideas and keep practicing. Whether future models will become indistinguishable from people, and whether machine-read documentation changes the judgment, remain open questions.
